pages.text:
Drills down to an oil deposit, then turns into a Well Head.
# Building
A 3x3 rig nine blocks tall:
- The floor: eight Derrick Casings round an open middle (the bore), with the Oil Derrick Controller in the middle of one side, facing out.
- Four Derrick Frame legs, seven blocks tall, on the floor's corners.
- A full 3x3 of Derrick Frames on top.
Keep the bore and the space above it open for the drill string.

Formed, it becomes a lattice derrick: four legs leaning in from the rig floor to the crown, girts and X-bracing between them, the drawworks and its engine house at the back of the floor, and the crown block's sheaves on the crown platform. The floor is a deck you can walk on (up the stair at its front), and the ladder up the front left leg climbs to the crown. While it drills, the kelly turns in the rotary table and the travelling block strokes down as the drawworks pays out line.

# Drilling
It drills a block every 2 seconds, using 120 FE/t and 10 mB/t of Water (drilling mud), and a Steel Pipe for every 4 blocks of hole, from its floor down to the deposit: to the top of its cavern under the bore, or to the deposit's depth in older chunks. Over no oil it won't start. Broken and rebuilt over the same hole, it carries on from where it was. The GUI shows how deep it is and how many pipes are still to come.
# Ports
A new rig has no ports: set them on its Derrick Casings with the Wrench in Port mode.
- Input: Water and Steel Pipes in.
- Energy: FE in.
# Striking oil
When it reaches the oil, the rig comes down: a Well Head caps the hole (drilled into a gas cap's dome, it's a gas well, for a Gas Wellhead instead of a Pumpjack) and the rig's blocks are left there to pick up, ready for the next hole. A Well Head can't be moved: broken, it's gone.
